methods.title: How we measure
methods.intro: Every claim on this page traces back to a real API response. Where we made a judgment call instead of measuring, it's named below.
methods.endpoint.skinAnalysis.name: AI Skin Analysis
methods.endpoint.skinAnalysis.use: Used to establish this is a genuine, distinct face per panel member (baseline skin-condition scores).
methods.endpoint.fitzpatrick.name: AI Fitzpatrick Skin Type Analyzer
methods.endpoint.fitzpatrick.use: Measures each panel member's Fitzpatrick band (I-VI). This is the band shown on every tile — measured, not assigned.
methods.endpoint.colorTones.name: AI Facial Color Tones Analyzer
methods.endpoint.colorTones.use: Measures each panel member's skin color as a hex value — the reference color the garment's contrast is checked against.
methods.endpoint.vto.name: AI Clothes Virtual Try-On
methods.endpoint.vto.use: Renders the actual product on each panel member. This is the image in every tile.
methods.sampleP1Measured: Fitzpatrick I, III, IV and VI
methods.sampleP1Gap: Fitzpatrick II and V are not measurable with this panel
methods.sampleP1Tail: — not covered, not claimed as covered, just not in this eight. We prompted for all six bands when generating the panel; the real measurement landed on four. That gap is disclosed here, not smoothed over.
methods.sampleP2Bold: Eight people are a sample, not a population.
methods.sampleP2Tail: This product measures whether a colorway separates from these eight measured skin tones, not what any population of customers looks like.
methods.provenanceBody: All eight reference images are AI-generated (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) — fictional people, not real individuals, not photographs of anyone. We chose this over sourcing real photos to avoid a likeness/consent problem entirely rather than manage one.
methods.thresholdHeading: Contrast diagnosis: how the threshold was chosen
methods.thresholdP1Tail: — the CIELAB luminance difference between the garment color and a panel member's measured skin tone. CIEDE2000 (ΔE) is shown alongside as a secondary, supporting number; the "loses contrast" claim is driven by ΔL*, not ΔE, because luminance separation is what the eye reads as an edge between garment and skin — hue or chroma difference alone doesn't guarantee that.
methods.thresholdP2Tail: We are not citing an external standard (WCAG, ISO, or otherwise) — this is our own operational cutoff for this product, and we're not asserting it as anything else.
methods.thresholdRationale: We call a pairing "low luminance separation" below ΔL* 15 — a threshold we set for this product, not a cited external standard. Below it, in our own viewing of the rendered images, the garment silhouette starts reading as a value-match to the skin rather than a distinct shape.
methods.garmentBody: Sampled by averaging a center crop of the clean, unworn product photo — not the composite try-on images, where background and each person's own lighting would bias the reading.
methods.limit1: Eight measured people; not a population estimate, not a demographic claim.
methods.limit2: The panel's measured Fitzpatrick coverage is uneven by construction, not by design intent — see the panel data's own coverage note.
methods.limit3: A garment's real-world contrast depends on lighting, fabric, and photography — this measurement is a comparative signal, not a guarantee of how the product will look on set.
report.title: CASTING — Coverage Report
report.measurableBandsBody: Fitzpatrick bands measurable with this 8-person panel: {bands}.
report.footnote: Eight people are a sample, not a population. Panel reference images are AI-generated (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image), fictional — not real individuals. ΔL* < 15 is this product's own operational threshold for "low contrast", not a cited external standard. Full methodology at /methods.
